open-question.question: When the completion procedure's discretionary read of past work fails — its `tasks <path> --with-body` call or its `show <milestone path>` follow-up exits non-zero, as `show` does on the `-` a task line prints for a commit joining no single milestone — what does the runner do: stop the task on a fixed line with the tool's `Error:` line beneath it, as the review pass and the starting-state procedure stop on a failed read of theirs, or carry on with the task without the read, as `ask-in-milestone-context` carries on after telling the failure in prose?

When the completion procedure's read of past work surfaces an earlier milestone's decision or verified bar that carrying out the task as briefed would undo, and the current milestone's `requirements.md` does not address it, what governs the work: the brief as written, the earlier decision wherever the brief can still be met, or does the runner stop without completing the task?

When the completion procedure's step-2 read of past work fixes a criterion of the acceptance bar, does that criterion name what it was formed against (the task commit's hash or the earlier milestone's path), so the read shows in the `Task-completion:` commit body, or is it worded like any other criterion with no reference to the read?

The completion procedure's read of past work is triggered by a file the task edits rather than creates whose shape the milestone's `requirements.md` does not explain. Does the same trigger cover a file the task deletes, renames, or moves?

The completion procedure's read of past work is triggered by a file whose shape the milestone's `requirements.md` does not explain. Does a shape the project's context file explains (in this repository, a `CLAUDE.md` invariant) count as explained, so that no read is taken, or does only `requirements.md` count?

With the milestones tool unchanged, does the completion procedure bound its `tasks <path> --with-body` read on a file that many task commits changed, or is the read taken whole whatever it prints? Measured on 2026-11-10 it prints 200 lines (59,079 bytes) for `docs/skill-reference.md` and 104 lines (31,521 bytes) for `CLAUDE.md`, and it grows with every later task that changes the file.

Does the completion procedure's `tasks <path> --with-body` read carry the clause the review pass and the starting-state procedure put on their milestones-tool calls — the command written out in full, never through a variable, alias, or function of the runner's own — or does it show the full command with no such clause, as the other nine runtime files calling the milestones tool do?

In the field measurement that decides whether the completion procedure's read of past work stays discretionary, which completion runs is the read counted against: every completion run, only runs that edited a file that already existed, or only runs a reader judges to have met the trigger (an edited file whose shape `requirements.md` does not explain), which no transcript shows mechanically?

In the field measurement that decides whether the completion procedure's read of past work stays discretionary, which outcomes are told apart for each counted run — for instance the named `tasks` command run as shown, a history read the agent composed itself (`git log`, `git blame`, or `git show` on the file), and no history read at all?

Over which runs is the field measurement of the completion procedure's read of past work taken: which projects and hosts, starting from which plugin release, and how many completion runs at the least before its result is read?

What measured result makes the completion procedure's read of past work a required step instead of a discretionary one: any counted run in which the read was not taken or was composed by hand, a stated share of the counted runs, or another rule?

Where are the scripts and the report of the field measurement of the completion procedure's read of past work kept, so that its figures can be checked again later: under the git-ignored `temp/`, where the reports and scripts of the two earlier field measurements stood and no longer do, in a tracked location, or does the plan in `ideas/milestones_addressed_by_path.md` leave it unstated?
